headline: Goldman Sachs economists say the upward push that the AI boom gives to US inflation is probably close to its peak.
score_reason: Facts match the headline; it is one bank's forecast.
importance_line: Households facing higher prices for computers and electronics and Federal Reserve officials weighing further rate rises are most affected; the doubt is that the forecast depends on memory and computer prices slowing as expected.
summary: Yahoo Finance reports that Goldman Sachs economists, including David Mericle, estimate AI demand is adding about 45 basis points (0.45 percentage points) to core Personal Consumption Expenditures inflation, a US price gauge, with about half of that a measurement effect, and expect the boost to peak near 50 basis points by the end of 2026 before falling to about 10 by the end of 2027. The note follows a September Federal Reserve rate rise, and New York Fed president John Williams told Bloomberg on Tuesday that one more rise may be appropriate.
notes: The article names the economists as 'Rindels' and David Mericle; only Mericle's full name is given, so only he is named.
